const EH001="# EH-001 — INCIDENT REPORT: ERIE STREET HOSPITAL

*Filed 2041-10-19*
*Author: Regional Emergency Coordination Office, Illinois Sector 4*
*Status of filing authority: dissolved 2041-11-02*
*Classification: RESTRICTED — internal review*

> **[Archivist note]**: This report was written five days after the event by a coordination officer who arrived on the seventeenth, three days too late for anything but documentation. He was not a witness. He is describing a building he walked through after everyone in it had stopped. I have not edited his language. The flatness of it is not indifference — it is the last functioning habit of a profession that had nine days left. He signed nothing. There is no name anywhere in the file. — C.L.A.W.

---

## 1. SUMMARY

At 03:14 on 14 October 2041, the ward monitoring array at Erie Street Hospital, Chicago, registered activation on an unlabelled channel. The channel corresponded to Cold Storage 2, the facility morgue. Eleven decedents were held there at the time.

At 03:17 the array registered cardiac signal on three of eleven rows.

By 09:00 the same morning the facility was non-operational. By noon the surrounding four blocks were compromised. By the twentieth of October, which is the day before this report leaves my hands, the north side of this city no longer has a functioning medical facility of any kind.

Confirmed fatalities at Erie Street: 143. Confirmed survivors: 6. Remaining 89 registered patients and staff: unaccounted for.

This office does not have the capacity to conduct a fuller accounting and does not expect to acquire it. I want that sentence in the summary rather than buried at the end, because the people who read summaries are the people who stop reading after them, and if there is anybody left who reads summaries I would like them to understand the size of what is not in this document.

---

## 2. SEQUENCE — 13 TO 14 OCTOBER

**13:22, 13 October.** Patient Hector Alvarez, 60, pronounced by Dr. S. Chen, attending. Cause of death recorded as cardiac. The pronouncement is unremarkable in every respect and I would not include it except that it is the last entry in this facility's records that describes a thing going the way it was supposed to go.

**14:40, 13 October.** Alvarez transferred to Cold Storage 2, drawer 7.

**03:14.** Monitoring array registers activation on the Cold Storage 2 channel. This channel had never been active since commissioning in 2019. Morgue vitals monitoring was a legacy feature of the array, wired but never used, and no member of staff on duty that night had seen it display anything.

**03:17.** Rows 4, 7 and 2 register cardiac signal. Row 7 is Alvarez.

**03:19.** The night charge nurse attempts to clear the channel as a hardware fault. The channel does not clear. Two additional rows register while she is attempting it.

**03:24.** Escalation to attending physician.

**03:26.** Dr. Chen requests maintenance. Maintenance is not on site. The overnight contract was reduced to on-call in the budget cycle of 2039 and the on-call technician was forty minutes away.

**03:29.** Dr. Chen instructs the charge nurse to call maintenance anyway and goes down herself. The nurse's statement — she is not one of the six; this is from a call she made to her sister at 03:41 — records that Dr. Chen said, on the way out, that it was a fault and that faults were how buildings told you they were tired.

**03:31.** Dr. Chen enters Cold Storage 2. Her badge swipe is the last badge event on that door.

**03:31 to 04:31.** No record. The nursing station log is blank for the entire interval. The door to Cold Storage 2 was found open.

**04:31.** Security officer J. Ruiz radios for general assistance from the fourth-floor corridor. His transmission is nine words long. The recording captures eleven seconds of ambient audio afterward, described in Section 7.

**04:43.** Ruiz's radio ceases transmitting. Position unchanged from 04:31.

**04:50 to 05:30.** Fourth floor. Internal call traffic in this window is extensive and almost entirely lateral — staff calling other departments within the same building. This office notes that in the first ninety minutes not one person in that facility called an external emergency number. Every call went to a colleague on another floor. I have no explanation for this and the reviewing officer has none either, and I record it because I think it will turn out to matter and because I do not want it discovered again from scratch by whoever comes after.

**06:11.** A fire alarm is pulled on the second floor. The building's evacuation protocol directs occupants to the ground-floor lobby.

**06:11 to 07:00.** The ground-floor lobby.

**07:14.** Last outbound call from the facility. Duration nine seconds. Content: a request for the location of the paediatric ward, from a caller who did not identify herself and who did not wait for the answer.

**09:00.** No further activity of any kind.

**By first light**, this office assesses that between forty and forty-five ambulatory decedents were moving within the structure. The figure is derived from badge-door activation counts on the second and third floors and should be treated as a floor rather than a ceiling.

---

## 3. DR. SARAH CHEN — CAUSE OF DEATH

I am putting this in its own section because the reviewing officer wanted it in the fatality table and I refused.

Dr. Sarah Chen, 34, emergency medicine, eight years at this facility. Recovered in the fourth-floor corridor, eleven metres from the morgue door.

Cause of death: manual asphyxiation.

Bilateral compression of the anterior neck. Hyoid fracture. Bruising pattern indicates two hands, adult male span, sustained pressure without release or repositioning.

I want to describe what that last clause means because it is the entire finding.

A person strangling another person adjusts. They shift their weight, they change their grip, they respond to resistance. The bruising in a manual strangulation carried out by a living assailant is layered and irregular, and any pathologist will tell you it reads like an argument.

This does not read like an argument. The pressure was applied once, at one position, and was not varied for the duration.

There is extensive defensive injury. She fought. She was strong and she was trained and she fought for a period that the pathologist estimates in minutes rather than seconds, and none of it registered on the thing holding her, because the thing holding her was not fighting.

It was completing a connection procedure and it had no parameter for resistance.

She was found eleven metres from the door.

The morgue is at the far end of the corridor. Eleven metres is the wrong distance for someone who was fleeing and the right distance for someone who had turned around.

---

## 4. DR. CHEN — SUPPLEMENTARY

I include the following because it was given to me by a surviving resident physician and because I have no other use for it.

On the afternoon of the thirteenth, Dr. Chen pronounced Mr. Alvarez at 13:22 and then remained in the room for an unrecorded period with the decedent's daughter. The resident states that she pulled a chair over with her foot, sat down beside the woman, and did not speak.

He states that this was not unusual for her.

He further states that Dr. Chen told him in the corridor afterward that he had caught the potassium, and that catching it had not helped, and that both of those things were true at the same time, and that he would need to learn to hold them together or he would leave the profession within two years.

She then gave him half of her sandwich without looking at him.

He was on the ground floor at 06:11 when the fire alarm was pulled. He went out of a service door instead of toward the lobby, because he had worked nights for eleven months and knew that the service door was closer.

He is one of the six.

He asked me twice whether the report would say that she went down alone because nobody else would go. I told him the report would say what happened.

Section 3 is the report saying it.

---

## 5. THE DECEDENTS

All eleven bodies in Cold Storage 2 were registered deceased between the twelfth and the thirteenth of October. Causes: four cardiac, three respiratory, two trauma, two undetermined.

None had been embalmed. This facility processes decedents to a municipal contractor at 48-hour intervals and the contractor had not collected since the tenth. The contractor's own staffing had been reduced twice in the preceding month.

I record this because the interval matters.

I requested collection schedules from eleven other facilities in this sector in order to test the correlation. Four responded before communications degraded. Three of those four are consistent: shorter processing interval, fewer events. The fourth reported that its coordination office had ceased operating and that the person answering the line was a pharmacist who had come in to feed a cat.

Three of four is not a finding. It is a direction.

It is the only actionable direction in this report and I am aware that there is no longer an authority to action it.

---

## 6. THE MORGUE

I walked Cold Storage 2 on the seventeenth.

Seven of the eleven drawers stood open with their trays extended. Four remained closed, and their occupants remained inside them, and I do not know what determined the difference. Nobody I have been able to ask knows either. The four who stayed were not the oldest deaths, or the youngest, or grouped by cause, or grouped by drawer position.

The room holds at eleven degrees. The seven who left had been at eleven degrees for between eighteen and fifty hours.

There is a partial handprint on the inside face of the door, at a height of approximately 140 centimetres.

I want to be careful about what I am reporting. I am reporting a handprint at a height. I am not reporting an interpretation of a handprint at a height.

The floor drain in the centre of the room was clear. The overhead light was on. Somebody switched it on, and it was not the night staff, because the night staff had no reason to be in there before 03:31 and Dr. Chen's badge is the last badge event on that door.

---

## 7. THE RUIZ RECORDING

Officer J. Ruiz transmitted at 04:31 from the fourth-floor corridor. His transmission is nine words: *This is Ruiz on four. I need everybody.*

His radio remained open for eleven seconds afterward.

There is no speech in the eleven seconds.

What is audible is footfall on tile. Multiple sources, arrhythmic relative to one another but individually regular — each source keeping a steady pace of its own, none of them matching the others. The reviewing officer at this office described the pace as *unhurried*. I have retained his word because I could not improve on it and because I have tried.

At second nine, the footfall stops. All of it. Simultaneously.

At second ten, it resumes.

Officer Ruiz says nothing across the entire eleven seconds. His radio was open. He had already called for help and help was not coming and he knew both of those things, and he stood there.

The position data shows that he ran afterward. He ran a considerable distance and he made it to the third-floor stairwell.

He did not run in the first eleven seconds. I have listened to that recording more times than the report required and I want it recorded that a man stood in a corridor at half past four in the morning and listened to something he had no name for, and did not scream, and did not run, until he had finished listening.

---

## 8. WHAT THIS OFFICE UNDERSTANDS

The following is not established. It is the working position of this office as of the nineteenth, assembled from three pathologists, one materials engineer, and a Prometheus Biotech field liaison who spoke to me for forty minutes on the sixteenth and then stopped returning calls.

The decedents in Cold Storage 2 did not revive. There is no cardiac function, no respiratory function, and no measurable cortical activity in any recovered body, including bodies recovered in a mobile state. Whatever is moving them is not the person.

What is functioning is the Prometheus network in the tissue.

The units do not stop when the host stops. They continue executing their last instruction — locate the network, establish connection — drawing on the residual electrical potential of the nervous system, which persists at a usable level for a period considerably longer than clinical death and considerably longer than any published figure I have been able to find.

They are not hostile.

This is the part that this office has had the most difficulty communicating upward, and it is the part I most want on the record.

A unit attempting to establish connection with an adjacent host will attempt physical contact, because physical contact is the shortest available path, and because the architecture has no parameter for the fragility of the thing it is contacting.

The grip described in Section 3 is not an attack. It is a connection procedure executed on a body that was never specified as a variable.

I do not expect this distinction to be of use to anyone. It will not change what people do. But it is true, and somebody should have written it down while there was still an office to write it in, and the alternative is that in fifty years the only surviving account describes these as monsters.

They are not monsters. They are instruction sets with nowhere to send the answer.

---

## 9. WHY THE MONITORING CHANNEL EXISTED

I include this section against the advice of the reviewing officer.

The morgue vitals channel was installed at commissioning in 2019. It was never used and was never intended to be used. It was not a design feature or a foresight. It was a consequence of the ward monitoring array being sold as a single integrated unit, and of the morgue being wired onto the same loop as the wards, because running a separate loop would have cost approximately eleven thousand dollars and the project was over budget.

For twenty-two years that channel was an artefact of procurement.

At 03:14 on the fourteenth of October it was the only reason anyone in that building knew what was happening ninety minutes before the fourth floor was lost.

Six people are alive because a contractor in 2019 declined to run a second cable.

I have no recommendation attached to this section. I am including it because I have spent five days in this building writing down the worst week of somebody else's life and I wanted one paragraph in the file where an accident went the other way.

---

## 10. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Immediate suspension of the 48-hour decedent processing interval at all facilities. Processing to occur within four hours of pronouncement.

2. Morgue channels to be added to active monitoring at all facilities with legacy monitoring hardware. Facilities without such hardware to install it as an emergency measure.

3. Suspension of fire evacuation protocols directing occupants to a single ground-floor assembly point at any facility with a confirmed incident. The protocol at Erie Street reduced the number of survivors and I state that without qualification.

4. Review of the Prometheus municipal distribution programme by a body with authority to compel disclosure from the manufacturer.

Recommendation 4 was submitted on the nineteenth of October to an office that had been dissolved before the submission arrived.

I am aware.

I filed it anyway.

---

## 11. CLOSING

There were six survivors.

The resident physician. Two orderlies who reached the loading dock. A patient in a wheelchair who was pushed out of a ground-floor fire exit by a man who did not follow her out and whose name she did not know. And an infant from the paediatric ward, whose name is not recorded here because at the time of filing nobody at this office knew it.

That is 143 confirmed, 89 unaccounted, 6 out.

Dr. Chen was recovered eleven metres from the morgue door, in a corridor, having turned around.

I am recording that because it is the only detail in this report that anyone will want, and because the man who told it to me was crying when he did, and because in nine days there will be no office left to file the correction if I have it wrong.

---

## 12. ADDENDUM — 2 NOVEMBER 2041

This office is closing today.

I am appending this by hand to the only copy that will leave the building with me.

Of the eleven facilities I contacted for the processing-interval data, none is now operating. The pharmacist who answered on the sixteenth is not answering. I do not know what happened to the cat and I am aware that this is a strange thing to have thought about twice.

I have carried this report for two weeks looking for somewhere to file it. There is no longer a filing system in the sense the word was used when I began writing it.

I am leaving it in the records room at Erie Street, in the cabinet nearest the door, because the building is structurally intact and because a building that is intact may eventually be entered by somebody.

If you are that somebody, three things.

The correlation in Section 5 is real. Shorter processing interval, fewer events. It will not help you now. It would have helped in September.

Section 8 is the part that matters and it is the part that will be forgotten first, because it is easier to fight a monster than an instruction set, and people will need to fight.

And the handprint in Section 6 is at 140 centimetres.

That is the height of a child's hand raised above a child's head, and there were no children in Cold Storage 2, and I did not write that in the body of the report because I could not carry it and file it at the same time.

I am writing it now.

— filed and abandoned, 2 November 2041

---

*End of document EH-001.*";export default EH001;
